solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: March with the beaten Allies' enemy

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are beaten, so these letters are whisked into a new order

parts.note: March and the are taken as written, with between them abbreviated to W, its standard short form

explanation.surface: A military march alongside the defeated wartime opponents of the Allies.
explanation.walkthrough: MARCH, W (with) and THE give nine letters, which 'beaten' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The German armed forces of the Second World War were the main military foe of the Allied powers.

clue.text: Blow or grass?

definitions.meaning: a wild swinging punch in boxing
cut and dried grass is turned into fodder, so grass cryptically produces that fodder; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: A puzzled query: is this thing a punch or a lawn?
explanation.definitionFit: A wild roundhouse punch has this name, and one who produces dried fodder from cut grass is cryptically the same word.

clue.text: Lover ascending before descent for nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lover of something is a fan of it
a descent is a fall

explanation.surface: A lover rising before falling, all for no gain.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF ALL is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang idiom means absolutely nothing, a milder form of a ruder phrase.

clue.text: Artist on a road taken in by sign

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the other pieces, as a guest is taken in by a host

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter on the road, taken in by a signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' here is a star sign of the zodiac, not a road sign, despite the road in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci, the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, is known by his first name.

clue.text: Show heaven is invisible

indicators.note: the word is is made invisible, so those letters vanish from the longer word

parts.note: paradise is heaven

explanation.surface: A claim that heaven cannot be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something off is to display it ostentatiously, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Remind, say, horse to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters climb, read from the bottom

parts.note: say means for example, EG
a dun is a greyish-brown horse

explanation.surface: Remind someone, for instance, that the horse must rise.
explanation.walkthrough: EG and DUN together are read upwards by 'to get up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a prod as a gentle reminder is a synonym of reminding them.

clue.text: A certain stone repeatedly defaced somewhere in the Himalayas

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its face, its first letter, so this happens twice

parts.note: a certain person is someone, one
an opal is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A particular gem, vandalised again and again, somewhere among the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE and OPAL each lose their first letter, the O, leaving NE and PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: This landlocked kingdom lies along the Himalayan range, home to Everest.

clue.text: Brave esteem, for what it's apparently worth

parts.note: to brave a danger is to face it
to esteem something is to value it

explanation.surface: Bold regard, offered at its seeming worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The worth printed or apparent on something, without looking deeper, is the idiom's sense.

clue.text: Encourage most of football team

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: Urging on the bulk of a football side.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To goad someone on, as a rider urges a horse, is a synonym of encourage.

clue.text: Help senior NCO to cut hair

indicators.note: the officer cuts into the other word, splitting it

parts.note: a mop is a shaggy head of hair
RSM is a Regimental Sergeant Major, a senior non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A sergeant major helping with a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: MRS MOP is old British slang for a cleaning lady; 'help' is domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is domestic help, and this nickname stands for any cleaning lady.

clue.text: Dance also interrupting one devoted to work

indicators.note: the linking word breaks into the other word

parts.note: a fan is one devoted to something
and means also
if something goes, it works

explanation.surface: A dance that also distracts a workaholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a verb here: a plan that works is said to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, done with castanets.

clue.text: Fish caught in flow by bank, almost

indicators.note: the letter sits within the word for flow

parts.note: a tide that is making is flowing in
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A fish landed in the current beside a riverbank, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: A tide is said to make as it flows in; RELY loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped oily sea fish of the North Atlantic, commonly smoked.

clue.text: Gather up a chain of rocks

definitions.meaning: sailors shorten a sail by rolling or folding part of it up
a ridge of rock or coral near the surface of the sea

explanation.surface: Collect a row of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in part of a sail and a line of rock under the sea share this nautical word.

clue.text: Censor is following crude study of public debate

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so these letters are roughly reworked

explanation.surface: A censor is pursuing a vulgar look at public argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' is not a positional signal but the abbreviation F, as in page references; 'is' belongs in the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of formal argumentation and debate is an older sense, from the Roman forum.

clue.text: By which a question is put about before bishop

indicators.note: the question word is put round the other pieces

parts.note: why is a question
ere is an old word for before
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A query raised about something going ahead of the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: This relative adverb means by means of which, the clue's own phrase.

clue.text: Europeans stopping one who disturbs game bird

indicators.note: the letters stop up the other word, filling a gap in it

parts.note: a beater flushes birds from cover on a shoot
E for European, twice

explanation.surface: Europeans halting someone who flushes game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British shoot, beaters drive game birds towards the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured insect-eating bird that catches wasps and honey-makers in flight.

clue.text: Old qualification secured by GI who's unknown

indicators.note: the outer word holds the others inside it

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, GI Joe
HND is a Higher National Diploma, a British qualification

explanation.surface: An old diploma held by an anonymous American soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: An HND is a British vocational diploma; GI Joe is the stock name for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: The placeholder name for an unidentified man in American legal use.

clue.text: Force 7 to approach prisoner about drug

parts.note: to near is to approach

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a convict
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Coming close to a convict, with drugs involved.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Beaufort scale of wind speed, force 7 has this name, a step below a full gale.

clue.text: Turn wife away from prizes

indicators.note: the wife is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: winnings are prizes

explanation.surface: Turning a spouse away from the prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a team's or batsman's turn to bat in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a player's or side's spell at the crease is their go, their turn.

clue.text: Girlfriend I put in minor role shunned by company

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside what remains
the company letters are shunned, left out of the word

parts.note: a cameo is a small acting part

explanation.surface: A girlfriend says she was cast in a bit part, then dropped by the troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMEO without CO leaves AME, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a female friend, borrowed into English for a girlfriend.

clue.text: When you get her over, you won't score

definitions.text: When you get her over, you won't score

parts.words: When you get her over, you won't score
parts.note: the surface hints at a failed romance, but in cricket an over bowled without a single run conceded carries this female name

explanation.surface: A rueful remark on a romantic conquest that goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; one from which no runs come is named for a young unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over with no runs scored from it bears this word for an unmarried girl.

clue.text: You can't enter this part of India, held by Koreans deployed after shelling

indicators.note: the Indian state is held inside the rearranged letters
troops deployed are spread out and rearranged
shelling strips the outer letters off the word

parts.note: Goa is a state of India

explanation.surface: A forbidden zone in India, held by Korean troops after a bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelling' removes the outer letters, K and S; the rest, rearranged by 'deployed', splits around the Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where entry is barred or dangerous, a forbidden zone.

clue.text: Shoot triggerman to the right of the heart?

indicators.text: to the right of the heart
indicators.note: the letters start at the very middle of the word and run on to the right

explanation.surface: A gunman told to shoot just right of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIGGERMAN has ten letters; its heart is GE, and the answer runs from there to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed's first shoot or sprout is an old sense, as in germinate.

clue.text: Not worthy of European to break strike

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the word, splitting it

parts.note: a blow is a strike

explanation.surface: A European unfit to break a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneath someone, as in below their dignity, is unworthy of them.

clue.text: In IKEA, try out one dish

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sampling a single meal at the Swedish furniture store.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed in a sweet soy marinade and grilled.

clue.text: Wrinkled flower digesting decapitated insect

indicators.note: the flower swallows the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a rose is a flower

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is lost

parts.note: a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: A shrivelled bloom eating a headless bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical and zoological term for a ridged or creased surface, from Latin ruga.

clue.text: Small deliveries, say, containing one new ruler

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: the two letters contain the numeral within them

parts.note: say means for example, EG
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Little cricket balls bowled, for example, with one new monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled; EG holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme ruler, a monarch, as well as an old gold coin.

clue.text: Cut joint without pressure

indicators.note: without means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a splice is a join of two ropes or pieces
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Cutting a joint of meat with no pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin piece cut from something, or the act of cutting it, as in a slice of bread.
